When I raved and rambled to friends about my Satay soup, another pal piped up and told me I needed to try the Spicy Lemongrass soup next! So, after a swim the other night, my friend and I placed a takeout order for two of those, and of course another order of GOC, which we promptly devoured in the car. The soup, however, was devoured outside of Legislature on a chilly-ish night, like an impromptu picnic. GUYS, I don't know which soup I like best now! I love the Satay for its layers of warm, savoury flavour, and the Lemongrass soup for all the veggies and variety of proteins. text: The service was excellent on this visit. Our server, Angela was very knowledgeable with the menu and helped me make detailed recommendations about which fish to have for the evening. Our drinks were refilled and plates were cleared regularly by all available staff and we were never waiting for a staff member to help us. When our food was delivered it went exactly where it was supposed to go without any auctioning. The complimentary smoked salmon and capers and champagne were a tribute to the success of the restaurant's one year anniversary and I very much felt a part of this. My service exceeded expectations. The lighting was perfect, without being too bright or dark. There was live music at the bar which was not too loud, and soft music in the dining room which was barely noticed. The temperature was comfortable, as I did not even notice it being too warm or cool. While the staff was clearing tables and taking orders, it did not detract from the experience, as each employee was fluid and efficient that many of these activities were not even noticed by guests. All employees were smiling and seemed to genuinely be enjoying themselves. The Crispy Oysters were served as five on top of the oyster shells. Each oyster was crispy fried and topped with a creamy glaze. They were extremely crispy on the outside, moist and delicious on the inside. The quality was excellent. The Truffle Macaroni and Cheese was served in a small boat with shaved black truffle and rich, creamy cheese. The top was slightly browned to add a slightly crispy texture. The quality was excellent. The Brussel Sprouts were served in a small boat and halved. They were garnished with small onion slices, bacon pieces, and caramelized for a crisp bite. They were slightly undersalted, however the bacon made up for this. They tasted fresh and were very good. The Swordfish was served hot on a hot plate. A warm crab salad sat on top of the fish, which was also topped with avocado. The swordfish had a steak-like quality, though was still flaky and moist throughout. The flavor was excellent and was perfectly seasoned. This exceeded my expectations. The Lemon Sole was served hot on a warm plate. It was browned and crusted with a Parmesan topping that gave a crispiness to the thin, delicate fish. The fish was still moist and flavorful inside the crispy casing. The fish, although thin, was long and met my expectations. The flavor and quality were excellent. The Bananas Foster Cake was served on a hot plate and lit aflame by the server who delivered it. The butter pecan iced cream had not yet melted and had a rich buttery flavor that paired extremely well with the banana buttercake. The cake was topped with fresh bananas with a side of butter pecan iced cream and whipped cream. The cake was creamy and rich in buttery, banana flavors. This dish exceeded my expectations and the quality was excellent.

text: Sonny's BBQ has always been a mixed bag for me whenever I have gone. Not enough to have you make an immediate u-turn out the moment you step inside, but it just doesn't seem to be a top priority. For example, there was water spilled all along the tiled part of the floor that no one had addressed before or after we left. The table at the front of the restaurant that had toothpicks and brochures was also dirty and covered in dust. Things like that. Our actual table we were seated at was fine though. The service was good. Our waitress made sure to check in and see how we were doing, but was never overbearing. The food always comes out quickly, which is what we wanted! Although on a side note, the table that was right across from us... the people came in before we did and apparently there was an issue with their order because they didn't get their food until we were just finishing our meal. The manager even came by to apologize - hopefully they got something taken off their meal because they were waiting a long time. But that seems to be the exception rather than the rule because Sonny's is QUICK to get your food out to you. I got the lunch portion of the House Dry-Rubbed ribs - the same thing I get every time! It has been awhile since I've been to Sonny's and I could have sworn this came with four ribs before, but now it is three. You also get your choice of two sidekicks - I got the fries and mac and cheese this time. Then you get your choice of cornbread or garlic bread - I got the garlic bread. The ribs were pretty good - not the best I've ever tasted, but they aren't bad either. You can eat them as they are, or they include three types of sauce at your table - mild, sweet, and smokin'. Since I had three ribs, I put a different sauce on each rib. Definitely my favorite is the smokin'... and I put that on my garlic bread as well! Fries are crinkle-cut and a little... dry? But once you dip them in ketchup, they taste better. The mac and cheese was just okay. I only had a bite or two of it. I wish I had gotten the corn on the cob or baked beans instead, which I know are delicious! This Sonny's BBQ has a drive-thru option if you want to get something to go. Never done it before, but might try it one day to take something back to work for lunch since it is just a few miles away. If you want a quick BBQ fix and are short on time, try Sonny's! text: I hate to be negative about this place because it would be a bit unfair. It is what it is and doesn't try to be something that its not....Except for the name of the place. I'll sum it up right here for what you should consider: This is the kind of place that a 20-something should come to if they just need a place to stay and don't want to spend a lot of money on a real hotel. It really is "Just a place to stay". I wanted to write this review so others would know and not get their hopes up. I thought the woman who worked there was nice. She let me check in early, and they really do mean well. But to be fair to everyone...this place isn't for everyone. We'll start with the fact that it's old and looked like a house that was converted into a "Hotel". With two large doors to enter, a delayed doorbell just to enter and four floors to walk without an elevator, be prepared and don't pack heavy stuff. My room was really two separate rooms from some time ago that shared a small bathroom. The rooms were small with noticeable wear, mainly no switch plates on an electrical outlet, window-mounted AC units and a sink that was pulled forward from the wall. The furniture was in good shape for it's age and a curious small corner closet would not open because the knob was missing (go figure). The room did have a flat-screen TV but it has the most basic cable ever. When I did locate the second remote, I could watch a little TV. I had a traditional key that opened my door as well as the front door, which is locked after 8 PM. OK.....Downstairs is The Monkey Bar, A nice enough corner bar with character. Seems like a nice place....for a 20-something to hang out in. Again I hate to bash this place because I do think they mean well, but "It's Not a Hotel....It's really a Bed and Breakfast....Minus the Breakfast". I was told there was no breakfast, but that there would be coffee with some pastries. I'm sure they were there because the day's table setting had them. There's free WiFi which was cool. The small shower was big enough with good water pressure. I had a small, dorm room-type refrigerator which I kept my free water and Dr. Pepper sodas. Even had a leftover of each from the previous person. The bed was comfortable enough and there was an iron and ironing board. I had towels which were fresh and shampoo and conditioner but no soap. Overall the place served its purpose for me, but it's not really for me. Costs a bit too much and is what it is and doesn't apologize for that. Again, don't mean to be negative, just need to people to be aware when considering this spot. It's just not gonna be for everyone.

Firstly, the physical location and space of Frew's Bridal is lovely and was a welcoming sight to behold post-sprint from my car during a summer thunderstorm. I left in good spirits, but the feeling was short-lived. A little over a week later I received a voice mail from a clerk at Frew's stating that they would not be able to get my dress in on time and I needed to pay them more money for a rush cut. I retrieved my receipt before I returned the call to indeed verify that I had paid for a rush cut already as was clearly indicated on my receipt. My return call to Frew's required speaking to three different clerks to verify that I indeed had already paid for the rush cut. Flash forward a couple of months and the other maids have received calls about their dresses (again different stories yet all the same) and I have yet to hear a status update on mine. A month before the wedding I call to see if my dress is in to be informed that it has been in, but no one ever called me. I was told to call an hour before I picked up the dress which when I later did was deemed to be erroneous (I would usually never remember such needless details, but I had been through too much already). I arrived to pick up the dress and asked for a fitting room to try on my purchase as I was uneasy with the standard of service exhibited thus far. I tried the dress on to find that it was about two sizes too big -- I know pattern measures can result in initial wonky fits, but no part of me came close to holding my dress up by any means whatsoever. I could not get out of the building fast enough as I know that the only "dieting" I did in the two months since the initial measurements and then was to switch from Tanqueray and tonic to Tanqueray and diet tonic -- no way I lost two dress sizes. I took the dress for alterations to a dress shop in my town which is owned by a friend of mine. My first fitting was met with laughter when I came out holding my dress on me. text: Land Ho!!!!! (This in no way should be considered as a slanderous mating call attempt used by lecherous pirates to pick up saucy wenches.) Welcome to Tampa in Late January, better known as Gasparilla pirate season when the cannons roar, the pirate ship sails up to the Convention Center, and the throngs of pirates take to the streets of Tampa in search of booty and grog. For well over 100 years, the residents of Tampa have celebrated the return of the legendary pirate Jose Gaspar and his band of merry marauders to the Tampa Bay area. Truth be told, the story of the pirate named Jose Gaspar seems to be more folklore than reality, but that hasn't stopped the residents of Tampa from dressing up and celebrating Pirate Days each year. The season kicks off with a Children's Parade one weekend, followed by the main Pirates Parade the next weekend, the Knight Parade through downtown Ybor City a few weeks later, and then the music festival, art festival, film festival, rum festival.... you get the picture. Most everyone shows up in costume, and you'll quickly assume that every woman who lives in Tampa must own a corset, short black skirt, and black boots. Unfortunately this is not the case at all, as you will also see many women wearing red & white striped tops and short black shorts. Many people arrive early to stake out their favorite viewing spots along Bayshore Boulevard, and wait for the afternoon parade. Still others pay an additional fee to have an elevated bleacher seat. While those in the know will pay even more to stand under one of the VIP tents and be offered free drinks, and access to very clean restrooms. At the appointed hour the crowds rush to the barricades along Bayshore Boulevard and perform the legendary "Throw me something, Mister!" gyrations while diving for strands of plastic beads. It is great fun, and definitely something that you need to do at least once in your lifetime. The parade is a little more bawdy than Mardi Gras, but not quite as bad as Fantasy Fest in Key West. For the past few years I've had the unique opportunity of viewing the parade from behind the scenes as a part of the City of Tampa's Office of Emergency Management. That has included some rides in the sky over the parade route, as well as the opportunity to walk the parade route before and after the actual parade. I've had the chance to see the good, the bad, and the positively ugly sides of this event, and had a lot of fun in the process. I have learned that anyone who shrieks "Woooo Hooooo" at the top of their lungs will likely be laying face-down on one of the side streets before the afternoon is over, and also that as the lines for the restrooms seems to grow longer and longer that people will find new and creative ways to water their neighbor's lawns. Thankfully most everyone is well behaved, and there are minimal problems with the partiers each year. This is definitely something that you need to see at least once. When else will you have the chance to dress up as Johnny Depp and approach a group of saucy wenches whilst saying your best pirate pick up line? "Arrrrgggghhhh, surrender the booty!"

text: TheDailyMeal.com recently posted an article on 101 Best Restaurants in America for 2015; Galatoire was ranked #22..... I've only come to New Orleans for work, so dining on my "to eat" lists are rare as I'm in back to back meetings, and often with others that do not necessarily have the same palette as I do. As you can imagine, I was thrilled to be able to convince a few colleagues of mine to check out Galatoire for dinner! Sure this place looks old school classy; imagine checked floors, waiters that invented what customer service looked like, and a suit jacket for all men during dinner service. Old school without the snobbishness factor.. I liked it! The food, let's just get straight to the point.. how was it you ask? -Galatoire Goute: A sampler of shrimp remoulade, crawfish, and crab. All three were dressed in a thick and creamy sauce.. imagine an overly sauced chicken salad but replace with Cajun/southern seasonings and replace protein with each respective seafood. I was starving so the crab worked, especially with a nice chuck of crusty bread. Shrimp's remoulade sauce was more of a creamy cocktail sauce that was unappetizing; the crawfish coated thickly was overly seasoned and remained on the plate unfinished. Of the three items, the crab was the most worthy, but that is already giving too much credit. -Lemon Fish: two colleagues ordered this, one topped with a lemon butter sauce and the other the same way but also topped with almonds. The fish was pan seared and cooked perfectly. Topped with a mild butter sauce and a nice squeeze of lemon to have the acid cut right through the thickness. A good fish if you're looking to steer away from the sauces, but nothing special about this entree. -Crawfish Etouffe: I expected more POW! More ZING! More FLAVOR BOMBS! Instead I got a consistency that was a touch thicker than broth, chunks of crawfish mixed with some stewed veggies, over rice. Not an expert on this dish, but I was indifferent about the flavors; nothing wow'd me but wasn't horrible either. Definitely not crave worthy Crab Yvonne: A sautee of lump crab meat, mushrooms, green onions, artichoke hearts, and a light butter lemon sauce. Add a squeeze of some extra lemon and enjoy! This was definitely one of the better dishes of the night! Turtle Soup: Not sure why I envisioned this to be a broth based soup, but was surprised when it came out and upon delivery it was more of a roux concoction. Deep flavor, and a bit salty after eating a few bites. Heavy and hearty, but very similar flavors to gumbo minus the rice. Good, but not great. Bread Pudding: Really, Yelpers?! As a highlighted thing to get, I have to SMH at you guys... it was a less cinnamony version of a cinnamon roll... aka just a chuck of baked dough with a thin praline sauce and a few slices of bananas. Sure, I like warm dough.. you got me.. and Yes I did eat it.. but was it worth the calories? Was it crave-worthy?! Absolutely not.. in fact.. a cinnabon sounds better at the moment! Overall, my taste buds were highly disappointed with my adventure here. #22 on the list in the WHOLE US of A in 2015? Bump it way down, TheDailyMeal.com, because you sir/mam are no longer a credible source for me.

text: The interior of 97 Hot Pot is exactly what I expected of a Chinatown restaurant. The decorations were minimalistic, Robert Morris would have been proud. It was a weekend evening and the place was PACKED; the food critic within me knows that for an all you can eat place, turnover is important, the more people who dine here, the fresher the food is. The second thing which hits all patrons is the smell. It is impossible to describe the smell: the restaurant has about ten different soup bases; range from the basic chicken stock (basic is free, everything else is $2 extra); to the fiery Szechuan Chilli stock, Ginseng Chicken stock, Chinese Medicine Combo stock. Now imagine about 100 individual hot pots, cooking 100 different ingredients; THAT is the smell which greets you when you arrive. Words cannot describe it properly, you must experience it yourself. This leads me to another one of those Alton advice, "wear disposable (or easily cleanable) clothes when you come to this restaurant", everything we wore into the restaurant will come out smelling a little bit of the restaurant. Imagine you clothes closed a sauna with 100 fragrant generating steam engines for 2 hours (yes there is a 2 hour time limit to this all you can eat festival). Fur coats and wool jackets are not recommended. My sincere compliments to the staffs, I have never seen a harder working group of restaurant employees before. As soon as we sat down, drinks orders were taken, then stock orders, then the countless rounds of food orders; OMG, each time food was ordered, the staff came back with it within seconds, fantastic service. Each person gets his/her own temperature control and individual hot pot, great concept, no need to worry about double dipping or reheating food. I know the raw food and the hot pot is the star of the show here but two things I do recommend you try is the Green Onion Cakes and Spring Rolls. Free unlimited supply and as good as most restaurants, freshly fried and arriving at your tables in minutes. The food quantity can be challenging. Meat wise, each order is a plate, about the size of a child's fist. Seafood wise, each piece is exactly that, a single sashimi style slice or a single shrimp. Tofu came in single tiny cubes, a friend ordered one tofu to try, expecting the a store size "brick" but it came in this tiny 1.5 cm X 1.5 cm cube, the staff gave us EXACTLY one tiny cube, we all had a great laugh over that. Noodles range from a tiny fistful to giant plates, no way to reliably order noodles that I can figure out. Veggies came in giant bowls, if you order any veggies, they come in a giant salad bowl which will last you all week and may be the next as well. The food variety was awesome, many different types of meats and meat balls. Two full pages on the menu with pictures for you to choose from. Seafood wise, shrimps, cuttlefish, OYSTERS and assorted seafood balls were available, but basa was the only fish. If you are hoping for fish, you may be disappointed. Why I capped OYSTERS?, because oysters in small letters simply will not do to describe these giants, they are the size of a tennis ball. They were delicious but one is enough unless you are an extreme oyster lover! A word to the garlic lovers or non lovers, there are a few whole cloves of garlic resting beneath each pot of stock; if you are on a date, especially first date, I recommend you fish them out early, over time, they melt into the stock and releases their wonderful aroma into the stock and everything you cook. If you are on a date and hoping for stage 2 afterwards, remove the garlics, lol. I love my garlic so I left mine but the quantity within each pot is a bit alarming. Back to the oysters, if you are hoping for stage 3,4 and beyond, order the oysters! Dipping sauce wise, there is the giant container of soy sauce plus chopped fresh green onions, cilantros and Thai chilies. Also an abundant selection of chili sauces and XO sauce. If you are more adventurous, the Chinese fermented shrimp paste, fermented tofu paste and other more exotic ingredients were present as well. I dare to say that it is unlikely any two individuals' dipping sauce is identical to another in the restaurant, we are all unique that way. After the all you can eat festival, ice cream, Chinese sweet tofu, Chinese sweet soup or some kind of Chinese sweet tea jello can be had. The only thing which puzzled me was the tea jello, not sure what is in it, it didn't taste like anything. When the bill came, the waitress made a point of saying that gratuity is not included in the $26 per person fee (with $2 stock charge, $3 per pop or $6 per drink) budget for $35 per person including tip. Not the cheapest Chinese meal ever but an all you can eat hot pot meal is definitely an experience everyone needs to experience at least one. Highly recommend

text: First, let me begin by saying I am not a cranky person. I always try and give people in the service industry the benefit of the doubt. I have been there once upon a time and I know how difficult it can be. That being said, when something has gone so terribly and obviously wrong, something must be said. Today, Mother's Day, my family and I dined at Cassis. Having been to the bakery many times and having heard many nice things about the restaurant, we chose it as this year's brunch buffet destination. I know, a buffet doesn't always allow for the highest in culinary excellence. I do allow for that. While I prefer a plated meal I do like the option of sampling many different types of food and generally reserve buffets for brunch. I believe the problem with this particular experience lay mostly in logistics. Whomever had the idea that this location could accommodate a buffet was so obviously concerned with profit margins over customer satisfaction it made me truly sad to know they are in the hospitality industry. Let me start off my rant by telling you that the bill for this comedy of errors was over $400.00. This included 5 adults and three children. All buffets I have been to include at the least, coffee, tea, etc. They charged us separately for every juice, coffee and soda we ordered. None of us ordered alcohol. It is hard to explain just how horrid the logistics were for this long, slow trudge up to the linen covered fold out tables that held our dried out pastries and obligatory cubes of cheese. The main dining room entrance is a pair of rather slim double doors. The genius behind this design decided to begin the buffet just inside these doors. The line began here which meant that while waiting in line for your turn you were one of the many, many people lined up single file stringing from the entrance, out the door and around the building. The velvet ropes circa every scene in a movie where a bouncer judges the worthiness of a club goer did not make the wait any more appealing. It was HOT. This is Florida, and standing outside, in the sun in "holiday clothes" flat out sucks. Throw in having any small children complaining about being hungry and it only gets worse. It was a very LONG wait. I guess this place doesn't have very many plates. When I arrived the plates had just been cleaned. They were hot, and I mean SCALDING. My daughter burned her hand and I myself had to play hot potato with them to tolerate the pain. This was the case for each person in my party and at different times. I was most looking forward to trying some of their baked goods as I had frequented the bakery before and been happy. A table containing many assorted pastries (muffins, fruit "Danishes", croissants, etc.) that looked promising, was not. Dry, hard and baked well in advance of a large crowd was all that came to mind. My selections went uneaten. We next came to an assortment of fresh fruit and cheeses. This was by far the highlight of my meal. The berries were big, fresh and full of flavor and paired well with their small but adequate cheese selection, save any cubal varieties. Next was a small table of lettuce and various toppings in plain white pasta bowls. This took up a lot of space on the buffet, and while fresh, this was lackluster. I would have much preferred to see some of the signature salads from the regular menu. I can throw beets and seeds on my spinach salad at home. Next came the wedding reception slab of prime rib/ham being carved by a very helpful, friendly gentleman. Unfortunately the meat had so much fat on it (even for prime rib), I skipped it. I guess that was the right choice, tasting it brought tears to my 4 yr old daughter's eyes (not the good kind) and I have never seen my father eat such little meat. Next, the all too familiar omelette station. I myself, am allergic to eggs so I did not avail myself. Although I can't imagine anyone else would wait for this after what we had all been through. Pivoting around brought me face to face with the cold seafood section. I wanted to cry at this point. An empty shrimp dish and two very skinny crab legs, was I supposed to wait for a refill with 50 angry patrons breathing down my neck? Some more hot food and a half empty pastry table and I was done. The pancakes were as hard and crumbly as the cookies I attempted in 3rd grade. After trying to juggle my kid's plates, by the time I got my own, everyone at my table was either done or had given up. I inhaled two mini tarts so as not to hold up the table any longer and got a "to go" soda. I felt bad for our very polite server who couldn't turn any tables. We were never greeted by any senior staff. I would have preferred to cook my family a meal than subject them to the reaping that was the Cassis buffet line. I felt duped; totally taken advantage of while imagining someone, somewhere counting piles of cash. People everywhere were grumbling, and the valet lost our car. A terrible first impression.
label: NEG

text: My son attended this Goddard School for over a year, but he has moved to a different school. Overall, while there are some good individual teachers at this school, the administration is a nightmare. The owner, in particular, seems to prioritize money over the best interests of the kids. The lack of professionalism from the owner and the administrative staff is a real issue--many months they wouldn't even have basic things like calendars available, or their communications would be inconsistent. One time they sent out an email about having a "desert bar" ... and had it spelled that way multiple times, so it wasn't just a typo. Is that who you want responsible for educating your child? Aside from all that, our son was diagnosed with some speech and socialization delays during his time at this school and entered Early Intervention. Both of his EI teachers visited his school and told us for his personal needs and learning challenges, the environment at this school wasn't right. Once we found a new school that felt like a better fit, we wanted to move our son right away, but the owner refused to let us leave without requiring dues to cover the full 30 days written notice, despite the fact that the enrollment agreement allows them to waive fees and let a student go if it is in their best interests (and we had a verbal conversation about it over 30 days before we left). For comparison, the school he moved to would have let him attend a few weeks for free just to help us do what was best for him. I wasn't surprised at all to see some other reviews on Greatschools.com that similarly echoed our experience--teachers are mostly good, but the owner/admin staff is not. And with the high level of staff turnover at these type of schools, you are relying on the owner to continually hire good people and hold them to a high standard. I would not trust the owner of this school to actually do that, at all. Basically, I wouldn't recommend this school to anyone. If your kid is a follower and fits in to a crowd, they'd probably do fine here, but you can find better. If your kid is at all unique like mine, this school has been generally unsupportive and not helpful, especially compared to his new school where the teachers and administrative staff have really gone out of their way to figure out ways to help keep our son engaged and included (that he has really responded to).

text: When I lived in St. Louis for 3 years, several classmates recommended Greentree to me. My preferred mechanic was all the way in my home state of Florida so obviously that wasn't an option. All of these things are things that I value. And it should be noted that they are more expensive than any other mechanic I've been to, BUT they are also located in a place with a higher cost of living and therefore, their average customer can afford to pay the higher price at the neighborhood auto shop. This isn't all that outrageous. People should not be shocked by this. So why would I give this place 2 out of 5 stars? Because there is a HUGE problem with the way they do business. After getting them to install a tow package in my Jeep, three weeks later, crap hit the fan in my Jeep Grand Cherokee and they did NOT stand behind their work--more specifically behind the part that they placed in the vehicle. The NAPA Balkamp product they placed in my Jeep malfunctioned and caused an electrical fire in my vehicle. It was pretty serious, and it could have been a lot worse. My home-town, mechanic in Florida and the GEICO insurance rep both took one look at the NAPA part and identified that the fire started because the part malfunctioned. The damage was around $2,400. The insurance covered all except the $500 deductible. My mechanic, Dave, said that I should contact the mechanic in St. Louis (Greentree) that installed the part to cover the deductible. Dave said that he personally does business and that is industry standard. Because when you install a part, you're taking responsibility for it as the mechanic and if it malfunctions--he as the mechanic will take that up with the Rep he bought the part from. Why? Because I'm his customer and he is the customer of the auto parts distributor and their sales team. Dave has stood by his work on our family vehicles in this way for 20 years. Which is why we trust him and recommend him to everyone without hesitation. I do NOT put this same confidence in Greentree. When I called Greentree, they didn't take care of me--their customer. They passed the buck along to their NAPA Balkamp rep: Michael Mann. They gave me his number and I called him. I emailed him photos and texted them to him as well. Haven't heard back from him since we spoke in October 2014. Why? Well, because I'm not his customer--he doesn't care about me. If Jeff at Greentree came to him and said, "Hey this part you sold me caused my customer a huge problem--here's the scorched part to show you," then you better believe Michael Mann would have gotten back to him. But not me. Therefore, I paid the $500 deductible and I contacted Michael on three separate occasions and he hasn't gotten back to me. So...if you go to Greentree, be aware that if they place a part in your vehicle that malfunctions and causes any sort of damage, they will pass you along to their parts rep instead of taking care of you like they probably should. The hardest part of it all is this: I don't think the owner would do this to his pastor or his pastor's wife--who are customers there at Greentree. I don't think they would do this to any of the several area ministers who are also their patrons. text: Tampa is has become quite the beer mecca in recent years and this has led to an abundance of Gastropub's for our imbibing and dining pleasure. Though most are located in trendy areas such as Ybor City and Seminole Heights, one of the best is located right near Bloomingdale. Tucked away in Kings Row Shopping Center under the big "PUB" sign resides the Stein and Vine which boasts a fantastic and constantly evolving row of beer taps and bottle options. The list is well balanced and the staff not only knows how to pour a proper pint (or snifter or goblet) but is also well versed in each offering. The Vine half of the menu is not as thorough, but is certainly more extensive and experimental than most any other local restaurant. The Stein and Vine will draw you in with the promise of a good drink, but will keep you there with astounding culinary offerings. Tater Tots have become a staple of many local establishments, but the Stein and Vine does them to perfection! I highly recommend the bacon and fried egg combo and a side of in-house chili. For a taste of something unique, the Pig Wings (a porcine take on tradition) with dipping sauce appetizer followed by an order of succulent Curious Traveler Drunken Shrimp that takes advantage of one of their more unique drink selections. Prefer something a little meatier? The 33 1/3 Cheeseburger is a half-pound burger that has a third of its mass made of bacon (that's right, 33% of their cheeseburger is bacon ...the word you are looking for is "OMG!"). The dining menu changes almost daily and the best way to keep up with it is to 'Like' the Stein and Vine on Facebook so that you can experience limited offerings such as Kentucky Beer Battered Grouper, Korean Mahi Tacos, or a personal recent favorite, the Breuben which is a House blended beer bratwurst w/ sauerkraut, house made remoulade & Swiss cheese on toasted rye. The one downside to the Stein and Vine is simply a lack of space. The bar is small and the dining area is packed tight. It is not uncommon to have to wait for a table and the location isn't exactly a restaurant row with alternatives. However, as of this review date, the owner has taken over the space next door which will effective double its size. But even with salvaged church pews lining the walls as a nod to the ancient brewing arts, I am sure the popularity of the Stein and Vine will quickly grow to occupy the addition.

text: I absolutely love this food. I'll say that again. I absolutely LOVE this FOOD. The chef and owners do an incredible job of bringing good quality Cajun inspired food to the Midwest. The Cajun gyro, which swaps out traditional lamb and feta for blackened lamb and bleu cheese, is downright amazing. The pat "say jack" with andouille and Tasso ham might be my single favorite sandwich in STL, packing all the saltiness, savoriness, and flavor of a proper andouille sausage with the bite of some Dijon mustard. And dirty fries. I'm just gonna stop there because you need them in your life. Again. I really truly love the food. However, after coming to this place time and time again, I can actually go ahead and say their service needs quite a bit of a wake up call. Now, some of the wait staff are more than friendly and I want to point out that I'm not trying to get anyone in trouble. But more often than not I have had truly awful service. Wait staff often seems upset that you're even in for dinner. I've had multiple experiences in which my table has been wiped down as I'm still finishing my meal as if I had already left. I've been stuck waiting for obscenely long periods of time after being seated and before being acknowledged and offered a glass of water. It's frustrating. Especially considering the first two or three times I came here, the service was incredible. The chef even came out of the kitchen to specifically ask me and my date how our food was and if there was anything else he could do to make our experience better. I never expect that from an establishment, so to have that initially was amazing. I'm not sure when or why exactly the service started to become so wildly inconsistent. Today I tried to call in to make an order for carry out, something I've done multiple times. The person who answered the phone promptly said they won't be fulfilling take out orders "right now". Okay? So I immediately came in and tried to place an order to go in person. I was greeted with a smiling hostess and a great experience at the bar while I waited. Seriously? It doesn't make sense. Some days I'll have pretty good service, but usually it will be terribly poor. Something absolutely needs to change though. Regardless of what has been said here, I persuade you, dear reader of this review, to come and try their food. It's worth coming in and bearing with service that will later be described by you and your accompanying party in a manner that can only be appropriately represented in a sample dialogue below: "Hey, how much are you tipping?" "You're tipping?" "I mean a couple bucks would be reasonable right?" "Not really. Our waiter made me feel like I offended him by having hands. He sucks as a waiter and a human being." Again, come eat their food. It really is amazing. I'll continue to come here often but with a major grain of salt if this service issue doesn't get resolved.

text: Stallworth was recommended for my mother's rehabilitation twice. Once from a liver transplant and the second a fall which fractured a rib and broke her humerus. Both within weeks of one another. The first time she was admitted she had rehabilitated well for the first 4 days then slipped on a downward spiral where she was shaking immensely and emotionally unstable. PT and OT could not find out why she did so well one day, walking 150 ft to not being able to stand. About the 8th night she was transferred back to the ICU at Vanderbilt for extreme dehydration and extremely ill. After being taken out of Stallworth, she started to walk about 12 hours later. We were discharged 3 days later and because of all the reactions she had had at Stallworth, we refused to go back. We found out when she was at home she was allergic to a diuretic mediation she was being given and 3 days later my mother has a fall and ends up at Vanderbilt again and we are convinced to take her to Stallworth. We had two contingencies, one was no medication other than what Vanderbilt has given without prior consent, and two, if we ever feel uncomfortable, we would be able to leave. Both wishes were not granted. The second time she had a bad episode of depression, anxiety, and pain the first night. Second night, she is fine and tonight, her 3rd night she calls me again informing me of chest pain and muscle weakness in her legs. I believe it may be another adverse reaction to a medication. We come to find out that Stallworth was giving my mother a medicine called Seroquel, a medicine given to bipolar patients or schizophrenic patients. The nurse supervisor, José gives me a run around and later refuses to inform me if she had taken Seroquel the night before. I inform him that she is not acting herself and is complaining of chest pain, but he continues to inform me that he cannot look at the chart now because his shift has just ended. We were on the phone off and on for a hour and a half with him claiming he would call me back in twenty. Forty minutes later, no call, when I call back he says he'll call back in ten. I never received a phone call back after he informed me of the medicine Stallworth gave her. I went as far as informing him that I would have to come over and pick her up which at that he said he would not allow me to come because visitor hours ended at 8 and he would call the cops if I showed up. Stallworth is not a place to take your loved ones. They do not respect the wishes of the patients nor the caregivers. They have their own team of doctors and prescribe their own medication despite what Vanderbilt doctors have prescribed, despite caregivers wishes of not wanting any other medication given other than what the primary team has prescribed. The PT and OT are wonderful but I would be very cautious of having your loved one there due to the doctor and nursing staff. My mother went from walking with no medical problems to extreme tremors, chest pain, and mood/behaviour changes while at Stallworth. As I write this review, my mother is at the Emergency room for the second time after being at Stallworth and given the medication she was not supposed to be taking. From research, many nursing homes prescribe Seroquel when they are short staffed to help patients sleep, but Seroquel can lead to very serious side effects sometimes leading to death especially in elderly patients. PLEASE BE SURE TO CHECK ALL THE MEDS ANYONE IS PRESCRIBING for your loved ones. A

text: This place is AWESOME!! My husband had been working hard all day...actually he had a very busy week...and decided he wanted to go to out for lunch. He didn't feel like going to any of our usual spots so I opened Yelp and started searching. I had this place bookmarked so we decided to try it, and we are so glad we did!!! We were greeted as soon as we walked in, Sarita was super friendly and very welcoming. We told her this was our first time here and she gave us a quick rundown of the menu and mentioned that all their flatbread was made fresh to order! Yum! The layout is really nice, the counter is to the left and the area to form a line is separated from the dining area so customers seated are not bothered by people walking back and forth. The decor was modern and hip, brick walls offset a deep brown wall. A very cool mural, great lighting and comfortable seating. My husband had the Texas BBQ & Bacon Cheeseburger and I had the Angus Beef, Spicy Buffalo & Blue Cheese Burger, we both added fries and a drink. My burger was sooooo good! The favors blended so well together, just the right amount of everything and the burger was so juicy! The flatbread was definitely fresh and so yummy! Sarita came by to see how everything was and my husband told her that this was his new favorite place! If you knew my husband you would know what a food snob he is haha. He is a VERY picky eater so for him to say that is impressive! The French fries were oh so yummy, cooked perfectly! And the sauces (fresh garlic aioli, home made thousand island and a hot sauce sorry I don't remember the name of it) were delish! I could not decide which one I wanted to dip my fries in, they were all so good! We are definitely coming back! Again and again! If your in the area you need to come here. If your not in the area you need to come here! Haha.

text: WHY BOTHER reviewing a shuttle bus service ? ! ? ! ? ! Well, it's simple... I just returned from a week-long vacation in New Orleans and I kept a list of all the services and businesses I used throughout the vacation; just figured I'd do them in order of each visit or use (with Louis Armstrong Airport to come later since I find this one simpler to write). Getting around in New Orleans (especially in or by the French Quarter) is a no-brainer... plenty of options (walk, city bus, tourism bus services, Uber, taxi and trolley cars)... but to get to New Orleans from the airport was the gray area I stumbled upon. Obviously a Taxi would cost a fortune (considering how crazy expensive they are, even for a simple 1 or 2 mile drive)... so my game plan was to request an UBER the minute I saw my suitcase come across the baggage conveyor belts.... I SEE MY BAG taken by some lady I recognize from the plane... she insisted it was hers but I had a "Yelp" Luggage Tag on mine and I said... "you ain't no Yelper, that's my bag".... I then open up the UBER app and... AND THEN.... STICKER SHOCK ! Turns out the airport has a deal with UBER to get a premium for pickups and drop-offs at Louis Armstrong Airport... $75.00 fixed rate to any of the French Quarter or Downtown area hotels... Yeah, SEVENTY FIVE DOLLARS ! UBER FAILED US ! We figured, what can you do... but on a whim decided to ask how much a shuttle service would cost at the nearest kiosk by the Baggage Terminal... When the lady quoted the cost to our hotel (Le Pavillon in Central Business District) I was thinking, "I think I misheard her"... I say excuse me and she repeated.... it was just $24.00 (Twenty Four) each person and that included the trip back too... in case you are not a math whiz, that's more than 100 dollars savings over UBER !) The process couldn't be any simpler... pay the lady behind the counter... roll or carry your bags out the door to the "Arrivals" which is also where all the shuttle buses are lined up... hand your ticket to the shuttle bus that is all the way at the front of the pack... the driver loads your bag into the rear baggage storage at the back of the bus... walk onto the bus and pick a seat... when all fourteen travelers on situated the driver will board the bus and takes your tickets and you'll be on the highway in a matter of minutes... the driver organizes the tickets in order of easiest path to drop us all off timely.... once at a tourist's hotel, the driver will unload your bag and back onto the road... DON'T FORGET TO TIP ! OUR EXPERIENCE (Airport to Hotel) I happen to be the last stop on our trip and the transportation was still reasonably quick... Our driver kindly pointed out some sites along the way and made some suggestions of what to do and what to see but for the most part we just stared out the window taking in whatever scenery we could... OUR EXPERIENCE (Hotel to Airport) And since the Shuttle service from the hotel back to the airport was included, they set up a time for us to wait out front of our hotel of 5:15 and even though there was a ton of traffic at that time, our driver still managed his time well enough to arrive only 5 minutes late... And will all the highway traffic, I thought we'd be late to the airport but the shuttle service has been doing this long enough to plan accordingly... and what do you know... just 5 minutes to the airport. Best part of our drive: our driver back to the airport shared a personal story of his family's ordeal when Hurricane Katrina struck the area... such a sad tale and when you hear someone tell you about the experience "from the heart" it's truly moving and you can't help but respect mother nature when she decides to flex her muscles... BOTTOM LINE: The only hiccup was I wish the luggage in the rear compartment of the shuttle bus had some sort of ticketing or "name confirmation"; as I was slightly concerned that someone from an earlier stop could claim our bag. It didn't happen but it's something they may want to improve upon. So my final thought... if you need a ride To and/or From Louis Armstrong Airport to your hotel... then this is your "hands-down" best option

text: Arrived at 5:35p for dinner. The restaurant seems to be disorganized. The Buffalo Chicken Tenders was served to us without the blue cheese and celery. The Fish N Chips were good, fries were crisp on the outside and the coleslaw was delicious. The Honey BBQ Melt Sandwich platter was delicious as well. We ordered the Crispy Chicken Salad which was not part of the 2 for $20 deal. $9.49 price does not warrant what we got. A very small portion of chopped chicken fingers, a large bed of brown edged greens and a very dry thinly sliced carrot as decor. All this and you get a very small portion of dressing. I am surprised that they are still open for business. One thing I will do mention is it took them 15 minutes for us to get our food which was a good wait time. We came because of the voucher we had. Other than that this visit is my first and my last.

text: Beware if you eat at this place with a large group! We called ahead to request a table for 17. We were informed that it would not be a problem. If you are required to retain receipts to submit to your organization, take note of this policy! Please note that speaking with a manager made no difference. We were given two different excuses: first, that their computer system could not separate checks more than 5 ways; and then, that there would be no way to separate checks for all of the 300 seats in this restaurant. All of this despite the fact that the restaurant is rarely asked to separate bills in this manner. After speaking with the manager and deciding that it wasn't worth the fight, we waited more than 30 minutes for the checks to arrive (all five of them)! And, of course, the 18% gratuity was already included. Stay away! The food's not that good anyway...
